title: Armenia and Azerbaijan finalize the text of a peace agreement
body:
On 13 March 2025 Armenia and Azerbaijan finalized the text of a long-awaited peace agreement. Armenia's Foreign Ministry said Yerevan had accepted Azerbaijan's proposals on the two remaining uncoordinated articles, which effectively concluded negotiations on the text. Azerbaijani Foreign Minister Ceyhun Bayramov said the negotiations had officially concluded and that the last two unresolved clauses had been addressed. Armenia proposed consultations with Azerbaijan on a signing date and venue.

Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan called the draft a compromise and said Armenia was ready to start consultations on the timing of signing. He said that after signing, the two countries would not deploy foreign forces along the border. The treaty would formally recognise each side's territorial integrity and establish diplomatic relations.

Azerbaijan said the treaty could not be signed until Armenia revised its constitution and legal framework to remove references to territorial claims over regions inside Azerbaijan, mainly Nagorno-Karabakh. Bayramov called this a necessary precondition for signing. RFE/RL noted that Nagorno-Karabakh had been under ethnic Armenian authority from the early 1990s until Azerbaijan's brief offensive of September 2023, after which more than 100,000 ethnic Armenians left.
